name: Security & Compliance Content Digest

parameters.content:
## Security & Compliance Content Digest

### Internal Protomated tool — Authority pillar, not deployed to clients

Solo and small firms rarely see plain-English security/compliance guidance written for their scale — most of what exists is written for enterprise IT departments. This is a content gap Protomated can own to reinforce the 'we never touch your legal work, and we take your data seriously' brand promise, feeding the newsletter/Field Notes content pipeline.

### How it works

1. Runs weekly. Pulls from a configurable list of public RSS feeds — breach-notification filings, bar-association security guidance, data-protection-law update trackers.
2. Filters to items published recently and matching relevance keywords (mentions of small/solo firms, breaches, compliance, data protection).
3. Drafts a plain-English digest entry per relevant item — a templated 'why this matters for small firms' blurb based on which keyword matched, not real analysis.
4. Logs the draft to a review ledger and emails it to the content reviewer. Nothing publishes without a human pass.

**This monitors and summarizes public information only — it is explicitly informational, never advice.** It never touches legal work, gives compliance guidance to a specific firm's situation, or drafts anything that could be read as legal advice (ABA Op. 512 doesn't directly apply since this isn't a law-firm-facing template, but the same discipline is kept regardless). Every digest draft requires a human review pass before anything goes into the newsletter pipeline.

### Setup steps

- [ ] Create a Google Sheet with a 'Digest Drafts' tab — see the deploy guide for exact columns.
- [ ] Configure Google Sheets OAuth2 and SMTP credentials.
- [ ] Set the required n8n Variables: SECURITY_DIGEST_FEED_URLS, CONTENT_REVIEWER_EMAIL, FIRM_FROM_EMAIL, DIGEST_LOG_SHEET_ID.
- [ ] Optionally tune RELEVANCE_KEYWORDS and DIGEST_LOOKBACK_DAYS.
- [ ] Activate the workflow.

### Customization

SECURITY_DIGEST_FEED_URLS and RELEVANCE_KEYWORDS are the entire content-sourcing surface — swap in real feed URLs (state AG breach notification pages, ABA/state bar publications, IAPP or similar data-protection-law trackers, if they publish RSS) rather than editing the code.

## Pull, filter, and draft the weekly digest

Reads a configurable list of public feeds, keeps only recent and relevant items, and drafts a plain-English blurb per item for human review.

nodes.name: Build Feed URL List
nodes.notes: SECURITY_DIGEST_FEED_URLS is the entire source list — a comma-separated list of RSS feed URLs (state AG breach notification pages, bar association publications, data-protection-law trackers).

nodes.name: Fetch Each Security Feed
nodes.notes: Runs once per feed URL from the list above, fetching that feed's current items.

nodes.name: Filter Relevant Recent Items
nodes.notes: RELEVANCE_KEYWORDS and DIGEST_LOOKBACK_DAYS control what makes it into the digest — most weeks this should still find something across multiple feeds.

nodes.name: Draft Plain-English Digest
nodes.notes: Runs once for the whole batch, not once per item — turns the filtered items into a single digest draft, explicitly noting when nothing relevant was found rather than sending an empty draft.

nodes.name: Assign Digest ID
nodes.notes: This ID ties the sheet row to this run — mostly useful if this template later grows a review/decision webhook like other ledger-based templates in this catalog.

nodes.name: Log Digest Draft For Review
nodes.notes: Every weekly run gets a row here, even a 'nothing relevant this week' one — a visible record of the digest actually running. Column headers must match exactly.

nodes.name: Build Digest Review Request Email
nodes.notes: The actual review task — an email with the full draft, since this catalog has no established task-management integration to open a real task in.

nodes.name: Send Digest Review Request Email
nodes.notes: This is an internal Protomated notification, not a client communication — no compliance guardrail wrap needed, same as PAC-76's internal review request.

parameters.content:
## Stale draft reminder — a second, independent branch

Checks the Digest Drafts log for anything still sitting at `pending_review` past a configurable age, and nudges the reviewer so drafts don't quietly go stale — mirrors the reviewer-nudge pattern already used elsewhere in this catalog (e.g. the conflict-check and case-study templates).

nodes.name: Check For Stale Digest Drafts Weekly
nodes.notes: Runs weekly, Thursday 9am by default — a few days after the Monday digest, so a draft that's gone unreviewed gets one nudge before the next week's digest arrives on top of it.

nodes.name: Read Digest Drafts Log
nodes.notes: Reads the full log — filtered down to stale pending drafts in the next step.

nodes.name: Find Stale Pending Drafts
nodes.notes: STALE_DRAFT_REMINDER_DAYS controls the age threshold — defaults to 5 days.

nodes.name: If Any Stale Drafts Found
nodes.notes: Only sends a reminder when there's actually something stale — no reminder email when the queue is clean.

nodes.name: Build Stale Draft Reminder Email
nodes.notes: Runs once for the whole batch of stale drafts, not once per draft — one reminder email listing all of them.

nodes.name: Send Stale Draft Reminder Email
nodes.notes: This is an internal Protomated notification, not a client communication — no compliance guardrail wrap needed, same as the main review request email.

nodes.name: Skip — No Stale Drafts
nodes.notes: Nothing to nudge about this run — every draft has either been reviewed or is still fresh.
